stata_command:
gen gsed_agemonths = int(el_gsed_age/10)
bysort gsed_agemonths: egen gsed_mean = mean(el_gsed_dscore)
bysort gsed_agemonths: egen gsed_sd = sd(el_gsed_dscore)
gen gsed_Z = (el_gsed_dscore-gsed_mean)/gsed_sd
variance_estimator: Sample standard deviation (ddof=1) within age band
analytical_notes: Age is divided by 10 and truncated toward zero with int(). Because age in days is strictly positive (739-1468 days), int() truncates to 10-day bands. Sample mean and sample SD (ddof=1) are computed within bands across the entire sample, not by arm. Five singleton age-bands (n=1) produce undefined SD and are left missing.

stata_command:
gen hv = arm_itt==2
gen afini = arm_itt==3
treatment_coding: hv = 1 if arm_itt==2 else 0; afini = 1 if arm_itt==3 else 0. Control (arm_itt==1) is omitted reference.
analytical_notes: Treatment is coded strictly by intention-to-treat (arm_itt). Control is the reference category (captured by intercept). No reclassification or dropping based on actual compliance or exposure.

finite_sample_correction: Student's t-distribution with df = G - 1 = 158 degrees of freedom
analytical_notes: Estimated via ordinary least squares with cluster-robust standard errors. Stata applies finite-sample degrees-of-freedom correction df = G - 1 = 158. Produces published Table 2 unadjusted results: HV 0.17 (0.04 to 0.30), Digital 0.14 (0.05 to 0.23).
Evaluates clustering of GSED outcome across communities. Intraclass correlation is approximately 0.032 (3.2% of outcome variance between clusters).

stata_command:
global covariates bl_childage child_female bl_low_bweight bl_z_overall bl_mo_age mom_sec mom_higher bl_f_b dad_sec dad_higher bl_fa_age bl_mics_tot bl_child_sib_tot bl_hhadults bl_qses_index
replace bl_f_b = 0 if bl_f_b ==. & bl_fa_age ==.
analytical_notes: Household structure is represented by TWO distinct variables: bl_child_sib_tot (siblings) and bl_hhadults (household adults). Father presence bl_f_b is set to 0 if missing when father age is missing. Mother education is represented by mom_sec (==4) and mom_higher (==5) with base <4. Father education is represented by dad_sec (==4) and dad_higher (==5) with base <4.

stata_command:
mi set wide
drop mom_sec mom_higher dad_sec dad_higher
mi register imputed bl_childage bl_low_bweight bl_z_overall bl_mo_age bl_mics_tot bl_hhadults bl_qses_index bl_fa_age bl_fa_educ_level bl_mo_educ_level
mi register regular bl_child_sib_tot cluster child_female bl_f_b
mi impute chained (regress) bl_childage bl_z_overall bl_mo_age bl_hhadults bl_fa_age (ologit) bl_mics_tot bl_qses_index bl_fa_educ_level bl_mo_educ_level (logit) bl_low_bweight = bl_child_sib_tot cluster child_female bl_f_b , add(250)
covariates_included: Predictors on RHS: bl_child_sib_tot, cluster, child_female, bl_f_b
cluster_variable: cluster included as continuous linear predictor in RHS
imputation_method: Chained equations (MICE): linear regression (regress), ordered logit (ologit), and logistic regression (logit)
analytical_notes: CRITICAL FORENSIC FINDING: No random seed was set before mi impute chained. Treatment arms (hv, afini) and primary outcome (gsed_Z) were NOT included in the imputation equations. Cluster ID was entered as a continuous linear predictor, not as fixed effects or multilevel random effects.

stata_command:
mi passive: gen mom_sec = bl_mo_educ_level==4
mi passive: gen mom_higher = bl_mo_educ_level==5
mi passive: gen dad_sec = bl_fa_educ_level==4
mi passive: gen dad_higher = bl_fa_educ_level==5
pooling_method: Computed identically across all imputed datasets
analytical_notes: Binary education category indicators are derived directly from the imputed integer education levels.

stata_command: mi estimate, post: reg gsed_Z hv afini $covariates, cluster(cluster)
variance_estimator: cluster(cluster) - CRV1 cluster-robust covariance within each imputation
finite_sample_correction: Rubin / Barnard-Rubin small-sample degrees of freedom
imputation_method: Multiple imputation pooled across M imputations
pooling_method: Rubin's rules for point estimates and variance combination
analytical_notes: Stata automatically restricts the estimation sample to valid gsed_Z cases (N = 2,149). All 15 baseline covariates are complete in every imputed dataset. Produces published Table 2 adjusted results: HV 0.17 (0.03 to 0.30), Digital 0.11 (0.02 to 0.19).

stata_command:
outreg2 using "Tables/table_impact_v2", replace excel ctitle(GSED - unadj) stats(coef ci) dec(2)
outreg2 using "Tables/table_impact_v2", append excel ctitle(GSED adjusted) stats(coef ci) dec(2)
finite_sample_correction: Reported stats(coef ci) with 2 decimal places (dec(2))
pooling_method: outreg2 exports pooled coefficients and 95% CIs
analytical_notes: The published paper Table 2 displays coef and 95% CI rounded to 2 decimal places.
